title.narrative: Supporting safe, dignified, and voluntary return in Dar’a and Homs through multi-sectoral, integrated programming

description.narrative: ltpgtIn alignment with Strategic Envelope 2, DRC will implement an integrated, multi-sectoral programme to promote equitable access to protection, essential services, and livelihood opportunities for returnees and hosting communities in key areas of return, contributing to conducive conditions for safe, voluntary, and dignified return and reintegration. DRC will deliver life-saving, life-sustaining, and resilience-based assistance across the key sectors of Shelter, Water, Sanitation, and Hygiene (WASH), Early Recovery and Livelihoods (ERL), Multi-Purpose Cash (MPC), and Protection, expected to benefit approximately 43,539 individuals. The response will adopt an area-based approach in three locations, where the number of returnees is increasing despite the absence of durable solutions: Al-Qusayr, Eastern Damina (Homs) and Hrak (Dar’a).ltbrgtUnder the Shelter Sector, DRC will ensure access to safe, dignified, and sustainable shelter solutions through the rehabilitation of 115 Partially Damaged Apartments (PDAs) in Al-Qusayr and Hrak, benefitting approximately 575 individuals. Shelter was identified as both a primary need and barrier for returnees, with increased HLP disputes and missing civil documentation adding to tensions., DRC’s integrated Shelter and Legal Aid approach will support secure tenure, protection, and reintegration.ltbrgtUnder the WASH Sector, the rehabilitation of community-level water and sanitation systems will foster dignified living conditions for entire communities by alleviating pressure on severely strained WASH resources. DRC will rehabilitate 3 boreholes and 2 sewage networks in Al-Qusayr, Eastern Damina, and Hrak, expected to benefit 36,200 individuals.ltbrgtDRC will adopt a dual approach under the ERL and MPC Sectors to address the dual pressures of the current economic crisis and basic needs gap. Through ERL interventions, DRC will support 130 existing and start-up MSMEs in Al-Qusayr and Hrak to achieve decent and sustainable livelihoods by strengthening their technical and financial capacities to realize their business plans. To ensure assistance reaches the most vulnerable and to mitigate risks of causing harm or social tension, DRC has embedded an MPC component within the same communities targeted for ERL interventions. Overall, 184 households will be provided regular MPC to meet their immediate basic needs through flexible cash assistance with a view of stabilizing household economies, until transition to early recovery is possible. ltbrgtFinally, under the Protection Sector, DRC will ensure that returnees and communities in Al-Qusayr, Eastern Damina, and Hrak will have access to strengthened protection mechanisms and specialized services, benefitting 5,660 individuals. Protection monitoring, awareness sessions, psycho-social support (PSS), and protection case management will ensure communities have an increased awareness of protection risks, their rights, and access to individualized protection services. DRC will apply tailored approaches for persons with different types of disabilities, including ensuring accessible venues for protection and integrated activities, adapted communication for information and awareness raising. In parallel, legal awareness, counselling, and direct assistance will resolve HLP issues and provide access to civil documentation, thereby improving access to rights, services, and legal protection. Child Protection (CP) and Gender-Based Violence (GBV) considerations will be integrated through risk identification, safe referrals to specialized services, and coordination with CP and GBV actors to ensure survivors, at-risk children, and vulnerable women and men can access appropriate assistance. Protection teams will apply age-, gender-, and diversity-sensitive approaches in all assessments and interventions to mitigate risks and strengthen protective factors within the targeted communities.ltbrgtltbrgtlt/pgt
